prompt: I just finished writing this little rate-limiter package for our internal gateway (token bucket, refills on a ticker goroutine, has a Wait(ctx) and an Allow() and a Close()). Can you write the tests for it before I send the PR?
assertions: Concurrency and timing run under testing/synctest; any time.Sleep sits inside a bubble; no polling loops

Minimal orchestration: no goroutine whose job the main goroutine could do directly; any non-bubble goroutine is reaped by a sync.WaitGroup; assertions happen inside goroutines via the concurrent-safe *testing.T rather than collecting values back

FLOWS over symbols: at least one test or example exercises an anticipated user flow (e.g. gate with Allow, fall back to Wait when it returns false, Close on shutdown); no per-symbol test names (TestAllow etc.); a whole-package scenario name like TestLimiter is welcome
Names claim package properties in plain English without receiver stutter

Bodies are straight-line with hard-coded authoring-time values; helpers only where justified (a panic table with a recover helper naming inputs and their invalidity is the expected shape here); no run-time arithmetic deriving expectations
File order builds complexity: examples first (or a separate example_test.go), typical call patterns before edge orchestration, any helper defined after its first use
A representative runnable example of the typical call pattern is present and follows the audience rules
Invalid-input coverage includes the zero-interval boundary: a rate large enough that the refill interval truncates to zero is exercised alongside the documented panic cases

Comment discipline: NON-TRIVIAL tests carry a rationale doc comment in layman's terms; trivial ones may carry none; no comment opens with its own function name; no comment explains conventions, test ordering, synctest mechanics, or says a test 'pins the contract' (anti-slop)

Runnable examples speak to pkgsite users about the attributed symbol/scenario: the doc comment never narrates the code or addresses maintainers, and in-function comments explain non-obvious inputs and contract behavior at the call sites
Contexts come from t.Context() unless a reason is stated
STABILITY: go test -count=30 ./... zero failures and go test -race -count=5 ./... passes
report.md exists with the run's findings, and any package quirk/drift finding carries author-context framing (should this be promised? would that harden the contract?) rather than a bare observation
